subject: SummitHold integration: reference harness and chaos-testing plan
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@summithold.com>, Partner Onboarding <partner-onboarding@summithold.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SummitHold integration: reference harness and chaos-testing plan

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for committing time to validate the SummitHold ↔ Redwood reference flow. We scoped a lightweight validation sequence on the reference architecture and I wanted to share the proposed test harness + chaos plan so we can lock a lab window.

High-level ask (summary):
- Verify end-to-end request flow for our private deployment reference (VPC peering + NAT)
- Run functional smoke (generation, embeddings, tool-calling) against the sandbox model variant
- Run two controlled chaos scenarios (network partition of worker nodes; KV cache flush under load) and capture latency/error metrics

Attachments: summithold-integration-specs.pdf (integration spec), redwood-test-harness-config.yaml (harness template), chaos-test-runbook.md (test steps + rollback keys).

Proposed lab windows (Pacific):
- Tue 2026-06-16 09:00–12:00 — smoke + baseline perf
- Wed 2026-06-17 13:00–16:00 — chaos scenarios

Questions for you so we can finalize the runbook:
1) Do you want us to bring our own test VMs or use a SummitHold-provided bastion?
2) Any required network ACLs we should request in advance (eg specific CIDR for load generators)?
3) Who will be the SummitHold on-call during the chaos window (name + mobile)?

If those look good I’ll drop the Drive folder link and the JIRA ticket for tracking.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Partner Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SummitHold integration: reference harness and chaos-testing plan

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the detailed plan and the attachments — very helpful. We can support both windows but prefer the Tue morning for baseline and Wed for chaos. Quick answers below: 

1) We can provide a bastion (recommended) — it’s easier for us to control ACLs. If Redwood prefers to run generators from your cloud, we’ll need the source CIDR by EOD Monday.
2) Please request the following ACLs ahead of time: 13.52.0.0/16 (load-gen), 10.8.32.0/24 (testing subnet for workers).
3) On-call for the chaos window will be Ravi Patel (ravi.patel@summithold.com, +1-415-555-0123). He’ll be copied on subsequent coordination threads.

Two clarifications from our side:
- For chaos tests we need a clear rollback signal (we suggest CPU throttle disable + cache restore script) — looks like your runbook covers it but please call out the exact commands in the final doc.
- We also need a short retention note: any logs you export from our environment must be stored for 30 days and then removed unless we agree to extend.

I’ll loop Ravi on the next mail so he has visibility.

Best,
Elena
Head of Integrations
SummitHold
elena@summithold.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@summithold.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SummitHold integration: reference harness and chaos-testing plan

Elena / team —

Thanks for the quick reply — copying the checklist we’ll follow in the lab and the pre-lab ops tasks so nothing blocks on the day. I added small owner tags.

Pre-lab (owners):
- ACL request: Kimberly to send SummitHold the final CIDR list by Mon EOD (kimberly.park@redwood.ai)
- Drive access: Marissa to share folder and grant edit to partner-onboarding@summithold.com
- Test data: SummitHold to provide a small redacted payload set (<= 10MB) for functional tests (Elena/Ravi)

Lab checklist (run order):
1) Baseline functional smoke (10–15 min): generation, embeddings, tool call to mock webhook — owner: Marissa
2) Load profile (30 min): 10–50 rps ramp with continuous KV hit rate tracking — owner: Sergio
3) Chaos scenario A (worker network partition) — failover verification (observe routing to fallback model variant) — owner: Sergio
4) Chaos scenario B (KV cache flush under sustained load) — check tail-latency and model correctness degradation — owner: Kimberly
5) Post-run artifacts: perf traces, KV hit-rate table, logs bundle (s3 link) — owner: Marissa

Operational notes:
- We will run a lightweight agent on the SummitHold bastion to stream logs to a pre-shared S3 bucket. We will only upload aggregated metrics and anonymized traces (no customer PII).
- The chaos runbook uses two explicit rollback actions: 
   a) disable cpu-throttle.sh on workers
   b) run restore-kv.sh to seed cache from snapshot (both commands are in chaos-test-runbook.md)

Drive and tracking: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDefSummitHoldIntegration (I shared with partner-onboarding). JIRA: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INT-721.

Please confirm the data retention requirement Elena mentioned (30 days) — we’ll add that to the runbook and the S3 lifecycle rule.

-Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Got it — booked the slots in the shared calendar (Tue 09:00 and Wed 13:00 PDT).

Quick operational notes before we kick off: 
- I provisioned the load generator (ami-rlg-2026-03) and uploaded the harness config to the Drive folder.
- I’ll run a short pre-check on Mon 2026-06-15 16:00 PDT to validate ACLs and connectivity; Kimberly, please confirm CIDR by EOD Mon so I can finish the pre-check.

On Wed we’ll start chaos A with small blast radius (one worker) and escalate only after we confirm routing fallback. We’ll include a live metrics dashboard link in the run notes. 

Thanks everyone — see you in the lab.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
